macro_events.event: July CPI: +0.1% MoM, +3.4% YoY; Core +0.2% MoM, +2.5% YoY
macro_events.causal_chain: Lower inflation → less urgency for Fed to hike → bond yields ease (10Y at 4.65-4.68%) → equity risk premium compresses → growth/duration stocks outperform → dollar weakens → EM and commodity-linked equities benefit. Second-order: mortgage rates soften marginally → housing sentiment improves (XHB, DHI, LEN).
macro_events.analog: July 2023 CPI miss that preceded the October-December rally as markets priced in rate cuts
macro_events.counterargument: Core at 2.5% still above the 2% target; services inflation remains sticky. One print doesn't make a trend — the Fed needs sustained evidence before pivoting.

macro_events.event: AMAT record Q3: $9.12B revenue, $3.50 EPS (beat), Q4 guide $10.25B/$4.02 — stock -5% AH
macro_events.causal_chain: Record revenue but priced for perfection → profit-taking in semis → rotation capital flows into software/cloud (WDAY, NET, MDB, PAYC) → semi ETFs (SMH, SOXX) face headwind despite healthy fundamentals. Second-order: confirms AI capex cycle alive — hyperscalers still spending — which benefits downstream software plays consuming that compute.
macro_events.analog: NVDA Q3 2024: record earnings but stock flatlined for weeks as multiples compressed; the rotation into adjacent AI beneficiaries (software, cloud) followed
macro_events.counterargument: AMAT raised guidance meaningfully (Q4 $10.25B vs Q3 $9.12B = +12% QoQ growth) — the sell-off may be a shakeout before continuation.

macro_events.event: Strait of Hormuz tensions: tanker attacks, declining vessel traffic, Iran exercises
macro_events.causal_chain: Hormuz disruptions → war-risk premiums on VLCCs → Brent/WTI spread widens → rerouting adds ~$2M/trip and 7-10 days → crude supply tightens gradually → energy producers (XOM, CVX, FRO) benefit, airlines (DAL, UAL) and transport face margin pressure. Second-order: if TTF gas spikes, European industrial costs rise → euro weakens → DXY strengthens (partially offsets CPI-driven weakness).
macro_events.analog: September 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent spiked 14% intraday before Saudi restored production in weeks. Current situation is slower-burn, more like 2023 Red Sea disruptions.
macro_events.counterargument: US SPR releases + OPEC spare capacity (2-3 Mb/d) can cap upside. Negotiations for Hormuz reopening are ongoing.

macro_events.event: China tariffs at 12.5%, negotiations for $30B product reduction framework, Aug 15 deadline
macro_events.causal_chain: 12.5% tariff below worst-case (25-40% was the prediction market range) → supply chains already adjusted → incremental impact muted. 'Agreed in principle' framework for $30B reductions → if realized, benefits consumer electronics (AAPL, DELL) and ag exporters. Aug 15 deadline creates binary event risk.
macro_events.analog: June 2019 Osaka G20 meeting — tariff truce sparked a multi-week rally before August escalation
macro_events.counterargument: Polymarket pricing 25-40% tariff rate by Aug 15 suggests market expects escalation, not de-escalation.
